question: Find CI on ₹1000 for 3 years at 10% p.a.?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The effective interest rate for **10%** compounded annually for **3 years** is **33.1%**.

**Compound Interest** = 33.1% of ₹1000

CI = (33.1 ÷ 100) × 1000 = ₹331

**∴ The correct answer is ₹331.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹1000

**Rate (R)** = 10% per annum

**Time (T)** = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

**Amount (A)** = P(1 + R/100)T

**Compound Interest (CI)** = A − P

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/939052f1502eb892c4e33db31a7550f718c66f10ff16d2585b7d33d1ee4ce125.png] 

⇒ A = 1000 × (1 + 10/100)³

⇒ A = 1000 × (1.1)³

⇒ A = 1000 × 1.331 = ₹1331

⇒ CI = 1331 − 1000 = ₹331

**∴ The correct answer is ₹331.**

**__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate for 3 Years

For a rate R%, the 3-year effective rate is 3R + (3R²/100) + (R³/10000) %.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years, Difference = P(R/100)². For 3 years, Difference = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

Compounding Half-Yearly

If interest is compounded semi-annually, the rate is halved (R/2) and the time is doubled (2T).
